Declare one parameter of a module or spec

Source: R/core-registry-schema.R
hr_param.Rd

A parameter states its type, default and allowed values once, so that the spec it belongs to is validated the same way wherever it is built. hr_validate() applies the rules; hr_schema() collects parameters into a schema.

Usage

hr_param(
  name,
  type = c("integer", "number", "string", "boolean", "enum", "string_vector",
    "named_map", "module_ref", "file"),
  default = NULL,
  min = NULL,
  max = NULL,
  choices = NULL,
  required = FALSE,
  help = "",
  cost_class = "none",
  affects_output = TRUE,
  tier = c("basic", "advanced"),
  evidence = NULL,
  depends_on = NULL,
  since = NULL,
  kind = NULL,
  strict = TRUE,
  resolve = NULL
)

Arguments

name

The parameter's name, as the spec field it fills.

type

One of "integer", "number", "string", "boolean", "enum", "string_vector", "named_map", "module_ref" or "file".

default

The value used when none is given.

min, max

Bounds for integer and number. Either may be a function of the parameters resolved before this one, for a bound that depends on another setting.

choices

The allowed values of an enum.

required

Whether a value must be given.

help

One plain sentence saying what the parameter does.

cost_class

How the parameter moves the cost of a run: "none", "local", "per_call_constant", "per_unit", "per_sample" or "per_round".

affects_output

Whether the parameter can change what a run returns, and so belongs in cache and store keys.

tier

"basic" or "advanced", for grouping in a user interface.

evidence

NULL, or a list saying where the setting comes from and whether its benefit has been measured.

depends_on

NULL, or a condition (a string) under which the parameter applies.

since

The version that added the parameter.

kind

For module_ref: the kind of module it names.

strict

For boolean: whether a value other than TRUE or FALSE is an error rather than FALSE.

resolve

NULL, or a function of (value, param, params) returning the resolved value, used instead of the type's rule. params holds the parameters resolved before this one.

Value

An object of class hr_param.

Details

The rules by type:

integer, number

A value that is missing, not a single value or not a number falls back to default, with a gr_bad_setting warning. With min or max, a value outside the range is moved to the nearest bound and warned about (gr_clamped, also of class hr_param_clamped). An integer comes back as an integer.

boolean

With strict = TRUE, anything but a single TRUE or FALSE is an error (gr_bad_setting). With strict = FALSE, anything but TRUE is read as FALSE.

enum

One of choices, matched as match.arg() matches, so an unambiguous abbreviation is accepted and the whole choices vector means the first choice. Anything else is an error naming the choices.

string, file, module_ref

A single non-blank string, or NULL when the default is NULL.

string_vector

A character vector, or NULL when the default is NULL.

named_map

A character vector, or a list whose elements all have non-empty names (an empty list is one), or NULL when the default is NULL.

A resolve function replaces the type's rule for a parameter that needs its own, such as an effort map checked against declared call stems.

See also

hr_schema(), hr_validate()

Examples

p <- hr_param("top_k", "integer", default = 6L, min = 1, max = 1e4,
              help = "Chunks to use.")
hr_validate(hr_schema(p), list(top_k = 8))$top_k
#> [1] 8

# Out of range: moved to the bound and warned about.
suppressWarnings(hr_validate(hr_schema(p), list(top_k = 0))$top_k)
#> [1] 1
